questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, a complete stop will:

options.text: Take a short amount of time.

questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate when air pressure gets too low. With a heavy load, stopping takes a long time because spring brakes do not work on all axles.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared by both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Only one side of the vehicle has brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: Heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. Each system has its own air tanks but shares a single set of brake controls.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor is connected to the engine by gears or a v-belt. It is cooled by air or by the engine cooling system.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should have:

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if carrying hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if driving through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers are potentially dangerous defects.

questions.question: When driving through a curve on the skills test, you should:

options.text: Leave your lane if needed to complete the curve.
Slow down after entering the curve.
Not look for other vehicles while turning.
Slow down before entering the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve so you do not need to brake or shift while turning. Keep the vehicle in its lane and watch for traffic in all directions.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you should:

options.text: Brake harder than in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra brake force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
Use less brake force than in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way as in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake an ABS-equipped vehicle the same way you would brake a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: When driving a new vehicle, learn the controls:

options.text: If you feel you need to.

questions.explanation: Learn the features and controls of a new vehicle before you drive it.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repair.
Safe if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Do not use wheels or rims with welding repairs. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: What does a safety belt do?

options.text: It keeps a driver safe during a crash.
It allows a driver to move around inside the vehicle during a crash.
It makes it hard for a driver to operate a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps a driver safe during a crash.
questions.explanation: A safety belt keeps the driver in place during a crash. This protects the driver from injury and helps them stay in control of the vehicle.

questions.question: During testing exercises, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position? (Do not count the straight line backing exercise)
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle twice to check its position during most exercises. For the straight line backing exercise, you can only exit once.

questions.question: When going downhill, when should you shift into a lower gear?

options.text: While you are going downhill and speeding up.
Near the bottom of the hill.

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before you go downhill. This prevents damage to the transmission and lets your engine help slow the vehicle. Choose a safe speed based on how steep the hill is, how long it is, how heavy your vehicle is, and the road and weather conditions.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent fatigue on long trips?
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Do not drive at night or when you would normally be sleeping, as this greatly increases fatigue.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see your vehicle?

options.text: Your headlights should be turned off during the day.
Your headlights should be covered with grease.
Your headlights should only be used in the rain.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean so they shine as brightly as possible. Clean lights help other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch the road ahead?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
It is not encouraged because it distracts you from driving.
It is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid a hazard.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach the hazard.

questions.question: Steering wheel play should be no more than how many degrees?
questions.explanation: Steering wheel play should not be more than 10 degrees (about 2 inches of movement on a 20-inch steering wheel). Too much play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: How often should you stop and take a break to avoid fatigue?
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: If you realize you will be late to your destination, what should you do?

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and accept delays. Drive safely at normal speeds. Plan ahead for delays when you schedule your trip to help reduce stress.

questions.question: On a wet road, how much should you reduce your speed?
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by about one-third on wet roads. Wet surfaces are slippery, making it harder to stop or turn, so you must drive slower.

questions.question: When parking in an offset back/right space, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space lines.

questions.question: What does the S-cam do when it turns inside a brake drum?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early. Signal well before a turn or lane change.
Signal continuously. Do not cancel a signal until the turn is completed.
Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't over-signal. If no one is near you, there is no need to signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before you turn or change lanes. Signal continuously throughout the maneuver. Turn off your signal after you finish. Always signal, even if no one appears to be nearby.

questions.question: While driving, your mirrors should be:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often while driving. This helps you know what traffic is around you. Mirrors also help you spot problems with your vehicle.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Turn the engine off as soon as possible.
Spray from the underside of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: In an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood. Spray foam through the louvers or from under the vehicle instead.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you should:

options.text: Plan your own route to show your skills.
Listen to directions from the examiner.
Bring a passenger to ride with you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen to directions from the examiner.
questions.explanation: Follow the examiner's directions during your on-road test. The examiner will never ask you to drive unsafely.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are located:

options.text: Only at the driver's side wheels.

questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are at all four wheels. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be:

options.text: Loose so it can shift when the vehicle turns.
Heavy enough that it won't move.

questions.explanation: Cargo on a flatbed or open trailer must be securely strapped down. This keeps it from shifting or falling off while the vehicle moves.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Always downshift before entering a curve in a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: A commercial vehicle must have all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Warning devices for a parked vehicle.

questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, warning devices like reflective triangles or flares, and a charged fire extinguisher. A flashlight is not required.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS:

options.text: Will still help you steer better.
Will let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will still improve your steering control. Watch your trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing out.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge or sign, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and take a different route if you can.

questions.question: ____ is a thin, clear layer of ice on road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it, which makes the road look wet instead of icy.

questions.question: Improperly loaded cargo:

options.text: Is unsafe but will not damage your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Cargo must be loaded properly for safety. Cargo that is not secured could fall and injure someone. Bad loading can damage your vehicle and make it hard to steer.

questions.question: When driving a truck that requires a CDL:

options.text: You never have to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if driving a tank vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: You must wear a seat belt at all times when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
questions.explanation: When crossing railroad tracks, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Alcohol usually:

options.text: Makes it harder to judge distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes it harder to judge distance.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your ability to drive safely. It slows your reaction time, makes it harder to judge distance, and reduces your night vision. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A cargo cover that flaps while driving:

options.text: Keeps the cargo cool by letting air through.

questions.explanation: Cargo covers should not flap while you drive. A flapping cover can tear loose and uncover your cargo. It can also block your view or others' views.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means the ABS:
questions.explanation: An ABS malfunction light means something is wrong with the Anti-Lock Braking System and it is not working correctly.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and motion for traffic to pass you.

questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, you must place emergency warning devices, such as reflective triangles, within 10 minutes.

questions.question: What color are the malfunction lamps on vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps. These lamps alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where your vehicle's lamp is located before you drive.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of the following do you NOT need to check?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.

questions.explanation: Check that your tires have at least 4/32 inch of tread on the front and 2/32 inch on other tires. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or over-inflated, and that all tires are the same size.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If this signal comes on while driving, stop the vehicle immediately and have the system repaired.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal followed by the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
Swerve from side to side to get other drivers' attention.
Turn all lights on and off several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash the brake lights.
questions.explanation: To alert drivers behind you that you are slowing down, tap your brake pedal lightly several times to make the brake lights flash.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, what will cause you to receive points against your score?
questions.explanation: The examiner counts each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time this happens, it counts as an error against your score.

questions.question: Are emergency brakes required on all vehicles?

options.text: No, not on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if nothing seems wrong.

questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on, stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible. You must stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, what lights should you use?
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.
